Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)  
- Assessment: Adult female presenting with a 2-3 day history of constant dull lower abdominal (below belly button) ache, nausea without vomiting, feeling hot and sweaty, and increased urinary frequency without dysuria or urgency. Reports recent resolved constipation. Last menstrual period approximately 3 weeks ago with anticipated period imminently. Reports pinkish discoloration in urine possibly representing light spotting. Sexually active on Implanon implant contraception. Allergic to Amoxicillin. No vaginal discharge. No systemic symptoms of dizziness or syncope.  
- Differential diagnoses consistent with clinical presentation include:  
 • Ectopic pregnancy or early pregnancy complications (High likelihood) due to abdominal pain, spotting, nausea, and contraceptive failure possibility despite patient’s belief pregnancy is unlikely.  
 • Pelvic inflammatory disease (Medium likelihood) given lower abdominal pain, feverish symptoms, spotting, and sexual activity but absent vaginal discharge and dysuria.  
 • Early urinary tract infection/cystitis (Medium likelihood) suggested by increased urinary frequency and systemic symptoms but lacking dysuria, urgency, or foul urine.  
 • Ovarian cyst or cyst rupture (Low to Medium likelihood) possible with abdominal pain and spotting but no severe pain or examination/imaging findings.  
 • Post-constipation related abdominal pain (Low to Medium likelihood) unlikely to explain systemic features given resolved bowel symptoms.  
- Examination and pregnancy testing urgently needed to exclude ectopic pregnancy and other serious causes.  
- Conflict noted: None identified between transcript and DDx; DDx appropriately supports and expands clinical reasoning based on presented history.  

Management Plan  
- Arrange urgent face-to-face GP consultation today for physical examination, including abdominal and pelvic examination, and pregnancy testing.  
- Advise patient to monitor for worsening symptoms such as increased abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, syncope, or systemic deterioration and seek urgent care if these occur.  
- Consider laboratory tests including full blood count and urinalysis as part of assessment.  
- Contraceptive counseling may be required pending pregnancy test results.  
- Consider pelvic ultrasound if pregnancy test positive or symptoms persist.
